questions.question: What does `npx expo start` launch?
options: The iOS App Store submission flow
The Metro development server, which bundles your JavaScript and serves it to the device
A web browser version of Android
questions.explanation: npx expo start runs Metro, the dev server that bundles your JS and prints a QR code so Expo Go or a simulator can load it.

questions.question: You save a change to a screen file and the phone updates in a second without restarting. What is this feature called?
questions.explanation: Fast Refresh swaps the changed modules into the running app, usually preserving component state.

questions.question: Your phone and laptop are on office Wi-Fi and Expo Go cannot connect to the dev server. What is a sensible first fix?
options: Run `npx expo start --tunnel` so the connection goes through the internet
questions.explanation: Many corporate or public networks block device-to-device traffic. Tunnel mode routes the connection through the internet instead of the local network.

questions.question: Which statement about the iOS Simulator is true?
options: It runs on any Windows laptop
It is built into Expo Go
It requires a Mac with Xcode, though you can still test on a physical iPhone via Expo Go from any OS
It is required before you can write any React Native code
questions.explanation: The iOS Simulator ships with Xcode, which only runs on macOS. Expo Go on a real iPhone works regardless of your computer's OS.
